newsitem.title: UK: Bomb alerts disrupt Britain's Grand National race.
newsitem.headline: Bomb alerts disrupt Britain's Grand National race.

text.p: Britain's Grand National horse race was disrupted by a bomb alert on Saturday after police said they had received two coded warnings of devices on the race course site.
Organisers began evacuating some 60,000 people at the race course after the bomb warnings were received some 30 minutes before the start of the race.
The buildup to the race was being shown live on British television when officials ordered the jockeys, horses and spectators to move out of the grandstands and away from the course.
Officials said police had advised them they had received two coded bomb warnings.

The security alert at one of the most famous steeplechases in the world followed the discovery of two Irish Republican Army bombs on motorways in central England this week which caused massive travel disruption.

The Grand National is one of Britain's major sporting events watched by millions of people at home and abroad. Officials said it was not clear whether or when the race, due to start at 1445 GMT, would start.
